title: Scientific trust and verification workflow
summary: Separates computed, converged, verified, and validated results while providing exploratory, engineering, and release policies for automatic runtime checks and campaign learning gates.

science.statement: A numerical result is accepted only through declared evidence; solver completion, discretization adequacy, reference applicability, implementation verification, and physical validation are separate claims.

equations.label: reference contract
equations.description: The reference, tolerance, and validity domain are stored with the decision.

equations.label: successive refinement
equations.description: A first convergence diagnostic; it is not silently presented as a full uncertainty estimate.

inputs.name: observable and reference
inputs.description: The actual value, expected value, and source of the expectation.

inputs.name: evidence policy
inputs.type: tolerances, validity domain, refinement sequence, claim kind
inputs.description: Defines acceptance before a result is promoted.

outputs.name: VerificationReport
outputs.type: JSON-safe claim collection and trust level
outputs.description: Passed, failed, and inconclusive claims plus the derived trust state.

assumptions: Reference values and tolerances are selected independently of the result under test.
Convergence samples represent the same modeled quantity and are ordered coarse to fine.
conventions: An inapplicable theory is inconclusive, not failed or passed.
A Golden value is a regression contract unless separate convergence evidence is supplied.
Validation claims require physical or experimental evidence and are labeled explicitly.
applicability: Release regression, analytical checks, metamorphic tests, mesh/time convergence, cross-solver comparisons, and simulation-to-learning admission.
limitations: The initial ConvergenceStudy does not yet calculate generalized GCI for arbitrary refinement ratios.
Trust evidence can be wrong if a user supplies an inappropriate reference; deterministic structure does not replace expert review.

validation_rules: Reject unknown trust levels and negative tolerances.
Reject unordered or shape-incompatible convergence samples.
Runtime claims cannot promote a result to verified.
Do not admit samples that lack an accepted requested quality policy.
